title: NorthStar POC — Infosec Evidence Packet and Audit Notes
content:
Executive summary:

This packet collects the responses, artifacts, and workshop notes we captured while running the NorthStar Financial POC (NorthStar) during Feb 2025. The customer requested a compact evidence bundle to support their internal vendor risk review. This document is organized as: 1) quick answers to the questionnaire sections they raised, 2) a checklist mapping controls to artifact files (S3 path or Confluence pages), 3) captured notes from the technical compliance workshop on 2025-02-12, and 4) open actions and owner assignments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Redwood Inference hosted API and Dedicated POC configuration used for NorthStar (no on-prem/private installs in this POC).
- Data classification: PII was not sent in test prompts; customer used synthetic data labeled as FIN_TEST.
- Evidence in S3 is redacted where required and marked with _redacted in filenames.

Quick answers to high-priority questionnaire items (for vendor risk):
1) Data residency and encryption:
   - All request/response traffic is TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) terminated at our front-door load balancers.
   - At-rest: model artifacts and customer-assigned caches for Dedicated instances are encrypted with AES-256 using KMS-managed keys. Evidence: s3://redwood-evidence/northstar/crypto-config.txt and Confluence page linked above.

2) Access control and IAM:
   - RBAC applied in Console: separation of roles between engineers, ops, and customer tokens.
   - Admin operations require 2FA and SSO enforcement via Okta in prod. Audit logs retained per standard retention policy. Evidence: audit-log-samples.csv (S3) and okta-config-export.json (redacted).

3) Network isolation and VPC/Dedicated tenancy:
   - For Dedicated portion of the POC we used an isolated GPU pool with private subnets and no public IPs for inference nodes. NAT egress was restricted via proxy. Evidence: vpc-arch.png and vpc-flow-logs-sample.txt.

4) Vulnerability management:
   - Hosts are scanned weekly with internal imaging and quarterly with third-party scanner (Qualys). Patch cycle: critical CVEs <=48h, high <=7 days. Evidence: vuln-scan-report-2025-02.pdf (S3).

5) Incident response and breach notification:
   - IR runbook exists and is linked in Confluence. SLA for customer notification: 72 hours for confirmed incidents. Evidence: IR-runbook-v2.md and incident-playbook.pdf.

6) Third-party/subprocessor disclosure:
   - Subprocessors: cloud provider (major public cloud), SSO provider (Okta), observability vendor for long-term metrics (Datadog). Contracts and DPA templates provided. Evidence: subprocessors.csv and DPA-template.pdf.

Artifact mapping (control -> artifact file):
- Encryption in transit: tls-cipher-report.txt (S3)
- Encryption at rest (KMS config): kms-key-policy.txt (S3)
- IAM configuration: okta-roles-export.txt (redacted), console-rbac-screenshot.png
- Network isolation: vpc-arch.png, subnet-config.txt, vpn-setup-notes.md
- Logging & retention: audit-log-samples.csv, log-retention-policy.md
- Patch & vulnerability: vuln-scan-report-2025-02.pdf, patch-calendar.csv
- Pen test/third-party assessment: pentest-summary-2024.pdf (executive summary)
- Data handling & retention: data-retention-policy.md, poc-data-flow-diagram.svg

Notes from technical compliance workshop (2025-02-12, 10:00–11:30 PST) with NorthStar infosec (attendees: A. Chen (Redwood), D. Martínez (Redwood), P. Shah (NorthStar), K. Adler (NorthStar)):
- Meeting objective: confirm evidence required for vendor risk grading and validate isolation controls used in Dedicated POC.
- Discussion highlights:
  * NorthStar required explicit confirmation that tokens and model KV caches for their tenant were not shared with other tenants. We demonstrated Dedicated configuration and showed cache namespace isolation. Action: provide cache-namespace diagram and a short write-up showing KV namespace assignment per tenant. Owner: Samir Rao, due 2025-02-21.
  * NorthStar asked about SOC2 scope. We clarified Redwood’s SOC2 covers the hosted inference control plane and certain operational systems; Dedicated hardware fleet may be covered under separate attestation depending on contract. Action: map SOC2 controls to POC scope and provide gap list. Owner: Priya Patel, due 2025-02-24.
  * Customer requested sample logs showing role-based access events for a recently executed canary deployment. We exported anonymized audit-log-samples.csv. Action: augment with timeline narrative. Owner: Avery Chen, due 2025-02-19.

Open items and owners (short tracker):
- Cache namespace diagram and tenant isolation write-up | Owner: Samir Rao | Due: 2025-02-21 | Status: in_progress
- SOC2 mapping to POC components (identify any missing coverage) | Owner: Priya Patel | Due: 2025-02-24 | Status: in_progress
- Annotated audit log export with narrative for canary deploy | Owner: Avery Chen | Due: 2025-02-19 | Status: complete (attached)
- Provide legal DPA sample with NorthStar redlines highlighted | Owner: Legal (Ana Ruiz) | Due: 2025-02-26 | Status: pending

FAQ / clarifications we gave during the workshop:
- Q: Are inference nodes single-tenant when Dedicated is provisioned?
  A: Yes, Dedicated GPU pools are isolated for the tenant requested in the POC configuration. Underlying hardware scheduling ensures no co-tenancy. Evidence: dedicated-attach-procedure.md.

- Q: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks from QA perspective?
  A: Model rollouts are controlled via the Console rollout system. Canaries are used for 1%–5% traffic before full rollout. Rollback is automated if error thresholds are exceeded. Evidence: rollout-trace-2025-02-03.json (anonymized), rollout-runbook.md.

Privacy note and redaction: all files in s3://redwood-evidence/northstar with _redacted suffix have been scrubbed of any customer-identifying PII. Original raw artifacts are available under legal hold only and require Data Access Request approval.

How to use this packet (for the NorthStar vendor reviewer):
1) Start with the quick answers above for the high-level checklist.
2) Open the mapped artifacts in S3 (links above) and the Confluence pages for runbooks.
3) For any gaps identified, escalate to redwood-security@redwood.ai with the ticket prefix NORTH-POC. We will route to the proper owner.

Contact list (POC):

- Dedicated infra lead: Samir Rao (samir.rao@redwood.ai)

Appendix: sample questionnaire responses (verbatim sections answered for vendor form)
Q: Please describe encryption for data at rest and in transit.
A: TLS 1.2+/1.3 protects data in transit to Redwood endpoints. At rest, customer artifacts (model snapshots, encrypted caches, and stored logs) are encrypted using AES-256 with keys managed by our KMS (customer-managed keys available for Dedicated contracts). See kms-key-policy.txt for key policy sample and tls-cipher-report.txt for cipher suites in effect.

Q: Where are logs retained and how long?
A: Audit logs for the POC are retained in our log store for 90 days by default, with the option for extended retention as a paid add-on. System metrics are retained for 30 days in hot storage and archived for 365 days in long-term storage. See log-retention-policy.md.

End of packet. If NorthStar or internal reviewers want a condensed one-page executive evidence summary, we can produce a signed PDF exported from Confluence. Requested next step: Priya to prepare SOC2-to-POC mapping and schedule a follow-up sync on 2025-02-25.
